newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crude firmer on rally after US strike on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Asia crude firmer on rally after US strike on Iraq.

text.p: Asian physical crude prices rose in tandem with the earlier rally seen on Brent and NYMEX futures after the United States fired cruise missiles on Iraq, traders said on Tuesday.
While brokers said the rally on crude futures has run its course on profit taking, other traders said they expect the surge to continue especially since NYMEX continued to rise.
They said regional grades particularly, might rise further as the full impact of the rally has yet to be felt.
Traders said three Dubai cargoes might still be available for October.

The Brent/Dubai spread for October was assessed unchanged at $1.75/$1.80. But some brokers said that with the rally on Brent, the October spread might have been discussed notionally at $2.40/$.3.00. Dubai intermonth spreads were steady to be offered at 45 cents for Oct/Nov and quoted 43/45 cents for Nov/Dec.
Traders said 500,000 barrels of Abu Dhabi Murban for October was confirmed traded between a Japanese trading house and a Japanese refiner at 12 cents a barrel over official quotes.
Sellers of Malaysia's Tapis said, after indicating October barrels at $22.40 earlier, they are now reasssessing it higher on crude rally.

Only one September Tapis cargo was left but "it has been reserved for something," a trader said. There were conflicting views on Chinese crude demand following the rally. A regional trader said China would be prompted to buy Minas in case prices rise further. Minas prices have been under pressure lately as China stayed away in anticipation of lower values.

But a Chinese trader said they were put off by the price spike and would stay away until levels dip. Traders now assess Minas premiums at parity to the ICP, up from minus 30 cents previously. --Ramthan Hussain, Singapore, (+65 870 3084), J. Oshima, Tokyo (+813 5473-3708)
